Project: PostgreSQL. Upgrade being assessed: 13 -> 16.
This change was introduced in release 14. Source: PostgreSQL 14 release notes: Migration to Version 14 (official_release_notes). Section: Release 14 / Migration to Version 14.
Version facts from package metadata for this release (authoritative for version numbers): none

ITEM:
<<<
Change EXTRACT() to return type numeric instead of float8 (Peter Eisentraut) This avoids loss-of-precision issues in some usages. The old behavior can still be obtained by using the old underlying function date_part(). Also, EXTRACT(date) now throws an error for units that are not part of the date data type.
>>>

PARENT CONTEXT (same section, for disambiguation only):
<<<
Release 14 / Migration to Version 14: A dump/restore using pg_dumpall or use of pg_upgrade or logical replication is required for those wishing to migrate data from any previous release. See upgrading for general information on migrating to new major releases. Version 14 contains a number of changes that may affect compatibility with previous releases. Observe the following incompatibilities: User-defined objects that reference certain built-in array functions along with their argument types must be recreated (Tom Lane) Specifically, array_append(), array_prepend(), array_cat(), array_position(), array_positions(), array_remove(), array_replace(), and width_bucket() used to take anyarray arguments but now take anycompatiblearray. Therefore, user-defined objects like aggregates and operators that reference those array function signatures must be dropped before upgrading, and recreated once the upgrade completes. Remove deprecated containment operators @ and ~ for built-in geometric data types and contrib modules cube, hstore, intarray, and seg (Justin Pryzby) The more consistently named <@ and @> have been recommended for many years. Fix to_tsquery() and websearch_to_tsquery() to properly parse query text containing discarded tokens (Alexander Korotkov) Certain discarded tokens, like underscore, caused the output of these functions to produce incorrect tsquery output, e.g., both websearch_to_tsquery('"pg_class pg"') and to_tsquery('pg_class <-> pg') used to output ( 'pg' & 'class' ) <-> 'pg', but now both output 'pg' <-> 'class' <-> 'pg'. Fix websearch_to_tsquery() to properly parse multiple adjacent discarded tokens in quotes (Alexander Korotkov) Previously, quoted text that contained multiple adjacent discarded tokens was treated as multiple tokens, causing incorrect tsquery output, e.g., websearch_to_tsquery('"aaa: bbb"') used to output 'aaa' <2> 'bbb', but now outputs 'aaa' <-> 'bbb'. Change EXTRACT() to return type numeric instead of float8 (Peter Eisentraut) This avoids loss-of-precision issues in some usages. The old behavior can still be obtained by using the old underlying function date_part(). Also, EXTRACT(date) now throws an error for units that are not part of the date data type. Change var_samp() and stddev_samp() with numeric parameters to return NULL when the input is a single NaN value (Tom Lane) Previously NaN was returned. Return false for has_column_privilege() checks on non-existent or dropped columns when using attribute numbers (Joe C
>>>

Decide the disposition:
- "risk": the item describes something that can break an app/deployment, require migration work, or create operational risk.
- "context": it is accurate but needs no action at 16 (no user action required, deprecated-but-working, additive feature). Give the reason.

For "risk", produce one or more risk paths. Use separate paths for separate symbols/APIs when they can be checked independently. Hard rules:
1. Every condition has at least one quote copied EXACTLY, character for character, from ITEM or PARENT CONTEXT (contiguous span, 3-40 words, no ellipses, no added words). Do not fix typos or formatting.
2. Each path has exactly one condition with category "version" stating that the upgrade crosses release 14 (quote the text that ties the change to this release, or the change statement itself), and at least one application/deployment condition (category api_usage, configuration, dependency, runtime, deployment, database, behavior or test_coverage) describing what the app or deployment must use/have for the risk to apply.
3. If the text does not state something you need, do not assert it: use role "uncertain" and explain in ambiguities. derived_by: "extraction" when the text states the fact; for an application/deployment condition ("the application uses X"), use "extraction" when the text names X as the thing affected by the change. Use "inference" only when you infer an affected symbol, scope or impact that the text does not name. Only add ambiguities for real gaps or conflicts in the text, not for the general fact that a specific application has not been inspected.
4. role: "required" (must hold), "alternative" (any one of the alternatives suffices), "optional" (raises impact), "disqualifying" (if it holds, the risk does NOT apply, e.g. not using the new opt-in API), "uncertain".
5. operator/expected_value must be checkable: e.g. operator "present" with expected_value the literal symbol; "less_than" with a version; "equals" with a setting value. expected_value is a string.
6. If a replacement API/setting/version is named, put the migration step in suggested_actions and add a condition for any behavior that differs in the replacement when the text states one.
7. search_queries: for app-side conditions with a literal symbol, give ripgrep regexes (tool "ripgrep"), kubectl commands (tool "kubectl") or SQL (tool "sql") that would find usage. Empty list if no literal symbol.
8. primary_symbol: the most specific identifier of the change (full apiVersion string like "policy/v1beta1", setting name, function, flag, or runtime name like "Python"/"Node.js"). symbols: all identifiers involved.
9. risk_level rubric: critical = upgrade fails or data is at risk for most users meeting the conditions (e.g. unsupported runtime/database version, removed API version that stops serving); high = code or config meeting the conditions breaks at upgrade; medium = behavior change or migration with a clear workaround; low = edge case, cosmetic, or warning-only.
10. fires_at: "upgrade" (at upgrade time), "first_use" (when a feature is first exercised), "rotation" (on credential/password rotation), "rollout" (on deployment rollout), "future_removal" (deprecated now, removed later).
11. applies_to: fill upgrade_method (e.g. "pg_upgrade", "dump/restore"), cluster_type, or from_versions (a version specifier like "<3.1") ONLY if the text restricts applicability; otherwise null.
Do not output confidence.

paths.path_name: EXTRACT() return type changed from float8 to numeric
paths.description: EXTRACT() now returns numeric instead of float8. The text says the old behavior can still be obtained by using the old underlying function date_part().

conditions.statement: The upgrade crosses release 14, where EXTRACT() changed its return type.
quotes: Change EXTRACT() to return type numeric instead of float8
conditions.relevance: Ties the EXTRACT() return type change to release 14, which is crossed by the 13 to 16 upgrade.

conditions.statement: The application calls EXTRACT() and depends on its float8 return type.
quotes: Change EXTRACT() to return type numeric instead of float8
conditions.relevance: The risk applies only where application code calls EXTRACT() and relies on the previous float8 result.
ambiguities: The text says the change avoids loss-of-precision issues in some usages but does not state which usages or result types are affected.

suggested_actions: Search application code for EXTRACT() calls and check whether the results depend on float8 return values.
Where the previous float8 behavior is required, use date_part() instead of EXTRACT().

paths.path_name: EXTRACT(date) errors on units not in the date type
paths.description: EXTRACT(date) now throws an error for units that are not part of the date data type.

conditions.statement: The upgrade crosses release 14, where EXTRACT(date) began raising an error for units not part of the date type.
quotes: Also, EXTRACT(date) now throws an error for units that are not part of the date data type.
conditions.relevance: Ties the EXTRACT(date) error behavior to release 14, which is crossed by the 13 to 16 upgrade.

conditions.statement: The application calls EXTRACT() on date values with a unit that is not part of the date data type.
quotes: EXTRACT(date) now throws an error for units that are not part of the date data type
conditions.relevance: The error applies only where EXTRACT() is applied to a date value with a unit outside the date type.
ambiguities: The text does not list which units are not part of the date data type.

suggested_actions: Search application code for EXTRACT() calls on date values and check the units used.
Ensure units used with EXTRACT() on date values are ones that belong to the date data type.
